decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through-glass vias are a core differentiated packaging-wafer capability that fits the firm's multifunctional packaging direction, even though recent web mentions are lacking.
Carrier wafers for smaller-diameter wafers are a low-cost extension of existing polishing and drilling processes and fit the stated reusable-carrier and thin-wafer handling strategy.
The Cu-interposer glass wafer is a flagship advanced-packaging technology launched at SEMICON Europa and aligned with growing glass-interposer demand, so the firm would keep developing it.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand reuses standard glass and quartz substrates with minimal extra cost and broadens the firm's market reach, making it a low-risk line to keep.

Glass-based circuit boards are far from the core business and carry a higher risk of being dropped, but they build on the firm's glass structuring and metallization know-how and support its interposer push, so keeping them still seems more likely.
